{"task": {"id": "I_kwDONElfw88AAAABXU4wUQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlV6PzhA4qjE", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlV6P", "number": 72, "title": "Allow collision between joint-connected MMD rigid bodies when collision masks permit", "body": "## Problem

The maintainer has occasionally observed MMD physics enter persistent violent oscillation, and is evaluating **one isolated physics change at a time**. The source/reference audit found a difference in how directly joint-connected rigid bodies are allowed to collide.

Current [`src/animation/MMDPhysics.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/src/animation/MMDPhysics.ts) registers every 6DoF spring joint using:

```ts
this.world.addConstraint( constraint, true );
```

The second argument to Bullet's `addConstraint` is `disableCollisionsBetweenLinkedBodies`. With `true`, the two directly connected bodies are prevented from colliding **even when their PMD/PMX collision groups and masks otherwise permit the contact**. The behavior was inherited from the legacy Three.js MMDPhysics implementation.

In contrast, several MMD implementations allow contact between joint-connected bodies, subject to collision filtering:

- [Saba](https://github.com/benikabocha/saba/blob/master/src/Saba/Model/MMD/MMDPhysics.cpp): `addConstraint( constraint )` (Bullet's default `false`).
- [babylon-mmd Bullet backend](https://github.com/noname0310/babylon-mmd/blob/main/src/Runtime/Optimized/Physics/mmdBulletPhysics.ts): `addConstraint( constraint, worldId, false )`.
- [babylon-mmd Havok backend](https://github.com/noname0310/babylon-mmd/blob/main/src/Runtime/Physics/mmdPhysics.ts): `collision: true`.
- [UMTNativePlugin](https://github.com/CandidumGames/UMTNativePlugin/blob/main/Source/NativeContext.cpp): `addConstraint( constraint, false )`.

[MikuMikuDance's supplied README](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-viewer-js/blob/master/model/default/readme.txt) explains the per-rigid-body **non-collision group** settings. However, no primary evidence establishes whether native MikuMikuDance additionally suppresses contact for every joint-connected pair. This is therefore a **focused compatibility experiment**, not a proven MMD-native correction or a guaranteed fix for instability.

**Risk:** For already-overlapping connected bodies, allowing collision can make contact separation compete with the joint's position/rotation limits, potentially increasing jitter or causing the very instability under investigation. The maintainer will evaluate the result with real models later.

## Expected outcome

Change only joint registration so PMD/PMX bodies connected by a joint **can collide when the existing collision group/mask filtering permits it**, by using `world.addConstraint( constraint, false )` (prefer explicit `false` for clarity). When group masks reject contact, those pairs must remain non-colliding.

Apply the same behavior to standalone synchronous physics, shared synchronous physics and Worker-owned physics, all of which construct joints through the shared `MMDPhysics` implementation. **Do not introduce a runtime toggle or A/B comparison UI**: the maintainer wants to try this single change and judge the visual result afterward.

### Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Change the constraint registration's `disableCollisionsBetweenLinkedBodies` argument from `true` to **`false`** in `MMDPhysics.ts`. Keep the joint frames, rigid-body geometry, default `STOP_ERP = 0.475`, spring parameters, constraints, body types and original collision group/mask configuration untouched.
- [ ] Demonstrate with **real Ammo/Bullet**, not just a mocked argument, that directly linked overlapping bodies can generate contact when both masks allow it; separately verify that a mask-blocked linked pair does **not** generate contact. Include an appropriate non-linked control, and verify non-contact constraint solving remains active. Use a small deterministic fixture and bounded simulation.
- [ ] Cover PMD and PMX metadata with existing/extended tests and validate synchronous, shared-world and Worker-owned paths as applicable, including relevant Type-2 synchronization regressions. Do not change physics behavior beyond this collision policy.
- [ ] Add a short note describing the actual Bullet semantics, the difference from old Three.js, reference implementations, and the **risk of increased vibration** for overlapping linked bodies. Do **not** claim the intermittent instability is solved or that native MikuMikuDance has been independently proved to use this policy.
- [ ] Do not mix in the other pending physics experiments: long-frame catch-up, STOP_ERP adjustments, damping tweaks beyond Issue #70, new recovery heuristics, or IK/type-2/body sync changes. Do not introduce public settings or a visual comparison switch for this trial.
- [ ] Report the relevant pre-merge checks: `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run test:browser`, `npm run build`, `npm run build:examples`, applicable real-asset/example checks and `git diff --check`. Automated tests may establish correct policy and lack of technical regressions, **not subjective visual stability**.
- [ ] All mandatory implementation and automated checks must be possible **before merging**; no published GitHub Pages state or manual visual review may be a pre-merge blocker.

### Required post-merge verification

After merge, verify the merge-triggered GitHub Pages workflow publishes the actual merge commit, and that the public PMD, Worker Physics and Gene Light PMX examples load without asset or runtime errors. Record workflow URL, deployed SHA/date and outcomes, and mark them **PENDING** until performed. Handle deployment failures separately.

The maintainer will **later review the real models by eye** (including whether contact makes movement more natural or causes additional instability) and decide whether to retain or revert this experiment. That manual review is optional follow-up and **must not block pre-merge PR approval or merge**. Do not represent automated passing tests or public content checks as a completed visual review.

## Context

- Prior independent physics changes: [#68 / PR #69](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/pull/69) (fractional Bullet time) and [#70 / PR #71](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/pull/71) (enable additional damping).
- [Bullet `addConstraint` API](https://github.com/bulletphysics/bullet3/blob/master/src/BulletDynamics/Dynamics/btDiscreteDynamicsWorld.h): `disableCollisionsBetweenLinkedBodies = false` by default. [Implementation](https://github.com/bulletphysics/bullet3/blob/master/src/BulletDynamics/Dynamics/btDiscreteDynamicsWorld.cpp) adds collision-ignore references only when `true`; [btRigidBody's reference handling](https://github.com/bulletphysics/bullet3/blob/master/src/BulletDynamics/Dynamics/btRigidBody.cpp) implements the ignore pair.
- The [mmd-parser PMD/PMX rigid-body parser](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-parser/blob/master/src/Parser.ts) reads each body's `groupIndex` and `groupTarget`, which the loader passes through to Bullet.
